findings.statement: The same-space no-go is proved. For I=<1-xi>, every finite constant-coefficient polynomial combination of the supplied terminal-vanishing basis lies in I, while rem_I(1)=1. If p_star*xi/(1-xi) equalled v in I on a nonempty terminal interval, denominator clearing would require p_star*xi in I^2, but its remainder is nonzero. Thus the external PCR-DG wording is FAIL-AS-WRITTEN when the terminal-vanishing trial basis is also the invariant test space. Independently, the required local determinant and rational entropy vectors pass exactly: det(M)=w1*w2*r1*r2*(p1-p2)^2, the frozen determinant is 3/1225, and J*A=(28/125)log(36)>0. These bounded passes do not supply a uniform candidate theorem.
assumptions_used: Finite basis and finite coefficients independent of xi.
Every terminal-cell basis function has endpoint limit zero.
Exact equality means pointwise equality on a nonempty terminal interval.
p_star>0 and xi approaches 1 from below.
Polynomial certificate over QQ[xi], with no saturation or localization.
For the mass lemma, weights and densities are positive and nodes are distinct.
For entropy, occupations lie strictly in (0,1) and the real logarithm is used.

findings.statement: The bounded fixed-lattice obstruction passes. With exact m_e=10219979/20000000 and delta_y=1/64, the mass indices at T=1 and T=6/5 are 10219979/312500 and 10219979/375000, both nonintegral. More generally, for any fixed positive delta_y, m_e/(T delta_y) is continuous and strictly decreasing, so it cannot be integer-valued on a nondegenerate continuous temperature interval. This is a necessary-condition no-go for fixed dimensionless lattices, not a sufficient four-momentum closure theorem.
assumptions_used: Exact positive m_e, temperature, and fixed delta_y.
Exact fixed-lattice closure requires m_e/(T delta_y) to be integral.
The FLRW temperature domain contains a nondegenerate continuous interval.
counterevidence_refs: The same exact output supplies delta_y=m_e/6 with indices 6 and 5 at the two rational temperatures, proving that the two-temperature sample alone does not kill every fixed spacing.
unresolved: On-shell momentum closure, nonnegative conductances, tail closure, and angular sparsity require separate proofs.

findings.statement: No moving-lattice/remap no-go is proved. The exact witness delta_y(T)=m_e/(64T) keeps the mass index 64 and therefore evades the fixed-spacing integrality obstruction. The registered inputs provide no theorem that such a remap preserves occupations, exact invariants, forward/reverse microreversibility, Pauli bounds, entropy, differentiability, covariance, and tail closure. ME-DVM admission is therefore INCONCLUSIVE rather than universally impossible, while its frozen fixed-lattice form is rejected.
assumptions_used: A temperature-dependent lattice spacing is allowed only for the scope test, not admitted as a design.
Every binding remap property must be proved before candidate admission.
counterevidence_refs: BD622_D039_second_external_audit_report.md states that remapping defeats the clean finite-state mechanism, but supplies no universal remap impossibility theorem.
reproduction: Inspect MOVING_SPACING_T1, MOVING_SPACING_T2, MOVING_INDEX_BOTH, and MOVING_SCOPE_CEILING in ext01_exact_checks.out.

findings.statement: PCR-DG novelty is not established. The registered proposal changes three plausible mechanisms relative to W6/B3-v2: half-line compactification instead of finite Y_max plus tail ledger, local cells/block masses instead of a global weighted-QR/Horner basis, and a generated single DAG instead of separate W6/W7/vector surfaces. But no complete PCR-DG operator or exact DAG comparison exists, so neither an isomorphism nor a non-isomorphism to B3-v2 is proved. A basis/domain description alone cannot satisfy the binding novelty obligation.
assumptions_used: Novelty is assessed against the sealed B3 basis, finite domain plus tail, mass solve, event trace, and A0-A4 graph as a whole.
A second language or a basis renaming is not structural novelty.
counterevidence_refs: The three proposed mechanism changes could be genuinely non-isomorphic if a complete operator DAG and consumer graph were supplied.
reproduction: Compare external report sections 8.4, 8.6, 8.7 with W6 sections 6, 8, and 10 under the CAS_CONTRACT novelty definition.
unresolved: Exact operator-DAG isomorphism or non-isomorphism certificate.

findings.statement: The binding cost obligation is not met by any registered candidate. ME-DVM has an exact proxy count of 34,504,704 edges at R=39,N_E=96,N_angle=1 and 621,084,672 at R=39,N_E=48,N_angle=12, an estimated 500-1000 design lines before evaluator code, and no credible deletion plan; it fails the registered cost screen. PCR-DG remains INCONCLUSIVE on cost because its 800-1500 evaluator/test estimate and possible net -600 to -1700 range cross both binding thresholds, and no exact same-change deletion plan proves permanent LOC<=800 plus net deletion>=1000. These are candidate-screen conclusions, not universal lower bounds on all sparse algorithms.
assumptions_used: Binding permanent implementation estimate must be no greater than 800 LOC.
Binding same-change deletion plan must yield net deletion of at least 1000 LOC.
The registered dense-edge proxy is R*N_E^3*N_angle^2.
Only registered-input estimates count; no speculative factorization is credited.
counterevidence_refs: A future sparse/factorized ME-DVM could beat the dense proxy, but no such registered derivation exists.
PCR-DG could satisfy cost at the favorable ends of its ranges, but no exact plan selects those ends.
